C0.quote: aggregating several rankings into one ranking

C1.quote: we give an axiomatic characterization of the Squared Kemeny rule
C1.note: AX: Thm 3.2, 3.3; AL: NP-completeness, ILP, approximation; WD/proportionality bounds in Sec 4 (distance guarantees); SI: Sec 6; SB: strategyproofness violated in Prop 3.4.

C2.3.note: Voters' preferences are mentioned: 'voter with a preference order'; in strategyproofness, input ranking is treated as preference.

C2.4.quote: how we compare two output rankings ▷1 , ▷2 based on an input ranking ≻
C2.4.note: Input rankings are used as preferences in efficiency/participation; rule applied directly; strategyproofness uses 'lying' vs truthful but without separate notation. Mostly input treated as preference.

C3.1.quote: requires that agents should never be better off by lying than by voting truthfully
C3.1.note: Only the strategyproofness axiom considers misreporting; other analyses don't.

C4.1.quote: disutility that the outcome ranking ▷ would give to a voter
C4.1.note: Satisfaction/dissatisfaction used (Sec 4 'average satisfaction of any group'); preferences over output rankings defined via swap distance to the input ranking, which is a specified link for efficiency etc. but utilities are not otherwise defined; coded PART.

C5.1.quote: We now provide a bound on the average satisfaction of any group.

C5.2.note: Evaluated on input rankings with no statement relating to held attitudes.
